lesson_title: Black Car, White Car, One Hour
hook_text: Two cars, same street, same sun. One hour later, one roof can burn your hand.
clip_script: The Sun's heat crosses 150 million kilometres of empty space as invisible waves. No air, no particles, just radiation. When those waves hit the cars, the black, dull roof soaks them up and heats fast. The white roof bounces most of them away. That is the whole rule: dark and dull absorbs, light and shiny reflects. Engineers use it everywhere. Solar water heaters have black pipes. Solar cookers bounce sunlight off foil onto a black pot and cook rice with no fire. Paramedics wrap people in shiny blankets that bounce body heat back. Choose your colour, choose your temperature.
visual_style: Whiteboard of the Sun with wavy arrows to a black car and a white car, arrows sinking into the black roof and bouncing off the white one, thermometers rising unevenly; then quick sketches of a solar cooker and a silver blanket.
pacing: Quick hook, a clear rule in the middle, a rapid list of uses.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build your own solar cooker.
